toegepas.blok: Nandi se dood en die rou
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'vir 'n tyd' follows English 'for a time'; ''n tyd lank' is the idiomatic Afrikaans form with the same meaning.
toegepas.rede_keurder: ''n tyd lank' is the natural Afrikaans form, the meaning is unchanged, and the protected 'Volgens een verslag' and 'sou lei' are untouched.

toegepas.blok: Nandi se dood en die rou
toegepas.rede_vinder: One 'kondig' a period of mourning 'af'; 'beveel' takes a command or a person as object, not a period, so the collocation reads stiffly.
toegepas.fout: 'beveel' with a period as its object is a loose collocation.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A ruler 'kondig' a mourning period 'af'; it is still his authoritative act, the protected 'routydperk' stays, and the next sentence carries the enforcement.

toegepas.blok: Shaka se dood en sy nalatenskap
toegepas.rede_vinder: The preceding sentence has the town KwaDukuza as subject, so 'Sy' reaches back two sentences; naming Shaka makes the reference (and the later 'sy leërs') clear.
toegepas.fout: 'Sy' follows a sentence whose subject is the town KwaDukuza, so it reaches back two sentences and could point to the town.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming Shaka fixes the reference without changing the meaning, the protected 'halfbroers', 'Dingane' and 'Mhlangana' stay, and it is not the earlier rejected 'sy leërs' change.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Nandi se dood en die rou
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Avoids 'afgedwing ... te dwing' in the same sentence; 'reëls opgelê' is the natural collocation.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Afgedwing' (enforced) and 'opgelê' (imposed) say different things, so the meaning moves.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Shaka se dood en sy nalatenskap
laat_vaar_vorige.na: terwyl Shaka se leërs weg was
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: After three other men are named, 'sy' could point to Mbopha or a half-brother; naming Shaka removes the ambiguity.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The sentence opens with 'Sy halfbroers', so the parallel 'sy leërs' clearly means Shaka; the change adds a repeated name without need.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Shaka se dood en sy nalatenskap
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Hul eie huis opsit' is the natural form of the idiom.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: ''n eie huis opsit' is already natural Afrikaans; the proposal is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Shaka se dood en sy nalatenskap
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: An apposition in running prose reads more naturally between commas than in brackets.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Brackets around a short apposition are correct and clear for a Grade 5 reader, so swapping them for commas is a lateral punctuation move.
